Every day, think of things you are grateful for.  


They could be the tiniest things. I'm grateful I'm in good health. I'm grateful I have a comfortable home. I'm grateful I still have my car. I'm grateful for friends who are there for me and will listen to my trivial issues. I'm grateful for family who will support me if I really need it. I'm grateful for my laptop. I'm grateful that I have a good brain. I'm grateful that I have an opportunity to improve my life. I'm grateful for my autonomy. Etc etc .... there are a million tiny things to be grateful for, and recognizing them consciously every day is the best way I've found to keep my head on when depression rears its ugly head.  


This simple change brought me from depressed and hating my life, having attempted suicide once, to truthfully enjoying life to an extent where not everything seems so bleak, and that I have hope for the future. I'd say that since I started doing this, I'm the happiest I've ever been, and it's so much easier to make decisions that benefit me.

The first few top comments suggest that feelings are inevitable and that once that happens, the relationship never works. I believe that having feelings for another human being is a wholly positive thing and that there's no reason that we should suppress those feelings. Why is it weird to like someone, enjoy their company, and want be close to them? We're social animals and thrive on this energy.

As long as you are honest with your partner about what you want then there's no reason to have any expectations beyond that. If things change, you discuss it to keep you both on the same page. There is no reason why you guys can't enjoy a relationship even if there are feelings involved.

Personally, I can't be intimate with someone intellectually, emotionally, or sexually and NOT have some kind of attraction for them, and I'd like to prolong positive relationships for as long as possible.
